opportunities.title: Small grants

amount.raw: Generally in a range of £1,500-£5,000; will only exceptionally exceed £6,000. Travel/subsistence in Japan up to £2,000 per person (trips up to 13 days) or £2,500 per person (14 days+); PhD fieldwork visits of 6+ months up to £5,000. Japan office up to ¥300,000 for PhD students.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants must belong to, or provide evidence of support from, an organisation or institution willing to receive grant funds. Not open to individuals for personal projects. UK-originating projects apply through the UK office, Japan-originating through the Japan office. PhD students must include a letter of support from their supervisor. No funding for consumables, salaries, materials, capital projects, student fees, undergraduate/master's students, or retrospective activity.
opportunities.summary: Seed funding for projects that bring people in the UK and Japan together to deepen mutual understanding, encourage exchange of ideas/expertise, or develop lasting collaboration. Supports festivals, workshops, performances, exchanges, collaborative projects, Japanese language/cultural studies teaching, and academic research/visits.

opportunities.title: Butterfield Awards in Medicine and Health

deadlines.raw: 1 December (decision in March of the following year)

amount.raw: Up to £10,000 per year; continuing projects lasting up to three years to a maximum of £10,000 per year, total limit £30,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to health and medical professionals, researchers, practitioners, policy makers, managers and voluntary sector workers in the UK and Japan. Projects must involve partners in both the UK and Japan. Applicants should normally show an existing research record; consideration also given to practitioners, managers, carers or others in health-related fields. Proposals must be supported by two professional referees from institutions different to the project partners. Preference to those new to UK-Japan collaboration and early-career applicants. Apply to the UK (London) office regardless of location. Cannot be used for laboratory consumables, salary subsidy, materials, capital projects or retrospective activity.
opportunities.summary: Annual awards supporting exchanges and collaborations between health and medical professionals in Japan and the UK, including study of scientific, clinical, social and economic issues in healthcare. Grants may be used for travel expenses or to contribute to other costs including conference and publication costs.
